content:
The [Random Team Generator](/team-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Shuffle a list of names into evenly sized random teams. Enter your one name per line, number of teams and seed (deterministic — for games/demos only) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Shuffle a list of names into evenly sized random teams. This free online random team generator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Random Team Generator

Start by typing or pasting your one name per line, then entering your number of teams and finally entering your seed (deterministic — for games/demos only). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Type or paste your one name per line.
2. Enter your number of teams.
3. Enter your seed (deterministic — for games/demos only).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Shuffle the names, then deal them one at a time across the requested teams.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Random Team Generator](/team-generator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

Here is a typical example. Six names across two teams produce two teams of three. ## What the result shows

With the default values (One name per line: Ada Grace Linus Margaret Alan Katherine, Number of teams: 2, Seed (deterministic — for games/demos only): 1), the [Random Team Generator](/team-generator) returns Team 1: Linus, Alan, Katherine, Team 2: Grace, Margaret, Ada. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Random Picker](/random-picker) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the units and labels before comparing results.
- Your entries stay in your browser and are not saved.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this random team generator free?

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or installation required. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Random Team Generator](/team-generator) and start straight away.

### Are my entries stored?

No. Calculations run in your browser and the tool does not save your entries. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What formula does the Random Team Generator use?

Shuffle the names, then deal them one at a time across the requested teams. You can see it in action in the [Random Team Generator](/team-generator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Random Team Generator?

Just One name per line, Number of teams and Seed (deterministic — for games/demos only). Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
